headline: Sales and profit surge to record levels, all segments up
summary_short: Caterpillar's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 24% y/y (18% q/q) to a record $20.54 billion, with adjusted EPS of $8.17 up 73% y/y as all three primary segments grew and operating profit jumped 50% y/y to $4.30 billion.
summary_long: Revenue rose 24% y/y (18% q/q) to a record $20.54B, driven by $3.1B of higher sales volume and $595M of favorable price realization; all three primary segments grew (Construction +35%, Resource +20%, Power & Energy +17%). Operating profit rose 50% y/y to $4.30B, aided by $392M of expected IEEPA tariff recoveries; adjusted operating margin expanded to 21.9% from 17.6%. Net income rose 65% y/y to $3.59B; adjusted EPS of $8.17 rose 73% y/y. Cash fell to $6.71B from $9.98B at year-end 2025 after $2.2B deployed for buybacks and dividends this quarter. No formal guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by $3.1B higher sales volume (mainly higher equipment sales to end users) plus $595M favorable price realization; all three primary segments grew.
Increase was primarily due to the profit impact of higher sales volume, plus $392M of expected IEEPA tariff recoveries recorded in the quarter.
Margin expansion reflects flow-through from higher volume and price realization, despite unfavorable manufacturing costs in Power & Energy (-$149M) and Resource Industries (-$158M).
Higher operating profit plus $398M of other income (vs $84M a year ago, mainly FX, swap contracts and investment income) drove the increase.
Management cited the first quarter ever above $20B in sales and revenues, pointing to strong order rates and a growing backlog across all three primary segments.
